Effects of Drug Addiction

In 2013, drugs killed nearly 50,000 people. Alcohol, the most deadly drug of all, claims almost 100,000 lives every year, with various addictions collectively costing the U.S. economy approximately $700 billion annually. Drug addiction might feel like a personal problem, but it’s a serious public health issue with far-reaching impacts.

blocks.text: If you’re struggling with an addiction to drugs, don’t lull yourself into a sense of complacency with vague reassurances that your addiction harms only yourself. Addiction is not a victimless act, and knowing just how far the consequences of addiction extend may encourage you to finally seek the help you need.

blocks.text: Emotional Effects of Drug Addiction

Drug addiction directly undermines your short and long-term emotional health. The effects vary depending on which drug you use, whether you have any pre-existing conditions, and how effectively you manage your psychological health. But some of the most common emotional effects of drug addiction include:

The effects vary depending on which drug you use, whether you have any pre-existing conditions, and how effectively you manage your psychological health. But some of the most common emotional effects of drug addiction include:

items.text: New or worsening depression or anxiety
items.html: New or worsening depression or anxiety

items.text: Feeling hopeless about your ability to get sober
items.html: Feeling hopeless about your ability to get sober

items.text: Intense cravings when you attempt to quit using

blocks.text: Physical Effects of Drug Addiction

Drug addiction is one of the surest and quickest ways to destroy your health. Different drugs affect your health in different ways. For instance, stimulants such as Adderall are more likely to induce heart attacks, while opiates such as heroin are more likely to slow your breathing. Some of the most common physiological effects of drug use include:

For instance, stimulants such as Adderall are more likely to induce heart attacks, while opiates such as heroin are more likely to slow your breathing. items.text: Organ failure, especially of the heart, liver, and kidneys

items.text: Chronic gastrointestinal problems, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach pain

items.text: Increased sensitivity to light and sound

blocks.text: Legal Effects of Drug Addiction

Drug addiction is almost always illegal, whether you’re abusing street drugs or illegally gaining access to more prescription drugs than your doctor prescribes. Many users suffer legal consequences, including:
blocks.html: Drug addiction is almost always illegal, whether you’re abusing street drugs or illegally gaining access to more prescription drugs than your doctor prescribes. Many users suffer legal consequences, including:

items.text: Loss of access to government programs such as student loans and welfare
items.html: Loss of access to government programs such as student loans and welfare

items.text: Incurring massive legal expenses, including attorney’s fees, bail, fines, and penalties
items.html: Incurring massive legal expenses, including attorney’s fees, bail, fines, and penalties

items.text: Loss of your right to drive
items.html: Loss of your right to drive

items.text: Being placed on probation and forced to submit to random drug and alcohol screenings

blocks.text: How Drug Addiction Affects Society
Drug addiction is more than just a personal or family problem. The effects of addiction extend outward to the larger culture, and include:
blocks.html: Drug addiction is more than just a personal or family problem. The effects of addiction extend outward to the larger culture, and include:

items.text: Contributing to organized crime, since a significant portion of drug sales are illegal transactions that fund gang or mafia activity.
items.html: Contributing to organized crime, since a significant portion of drug sales are illegal transactions that fund gang or mafia activity.

items.text: Playing a role in terrorism, since the opium that makes opioids such as heroin is the leading crop of the Taliban and Al Qaeda.
